thread:
Customer Support: Hey team — TesseractPay on Dedicated pool dp-prod-12 reporting a sudden wave of 429s and token/sec SLO violations starting ~10:10 UTC. Customer says traffic was a normal campaign but burst credits exhausted. They see spikes in latency too. Attach logs when available. :warning:

Priya (sre): Thanks — can you paste the auth/account id + exact timestamps? Any repro curl?

Customer Support: account: acct-TESS-921, window: 2026-03-15 10:08:00–10:22:00 UTC. Quick repro they ran: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` in a tight loop (~1200 req/s sustained for ~2m). They said initial response latencies jumped to 550–900ms and then started seeing 429s.

Priya (sre): Ok grabbing metrics — want TPS, tokens/sec, admission controller logs, and burst-credit ledger for that account. @ops-oncall can you check pool dp-prod-12 headroom and any autoscale events?

ops-oncall: Seeing a fast rise in active connections at 10:09. Autoscale attempted one scale-up at 10:11 but it failed to provision extra slots due to ephemeral GPU shortage in the AZ. Admission controller then began denying requests when account's burst credits hit 0 at 10:13. Logs: `admission: deny account=acct-TESS-921 reason=burst_credits_exhausted tokens=+0`

Priya (sre): Can you paste the admission controller policy for the pool? Also show burst credit balance changes.

SRE Bot: admission-policy dp-prod-12: {min_headroom_tokens: 4000, max_burst_tokens_per_account: 20000, refill_rate_per_min: 1000} (snapshotted at 2026-03-15T09:59Z).

Liam (eng-runtime): Interesting — the min_headroom looks high relative to request size distribution. If many small requests come in, wasteful headroom can cause early rejects. Also autoscaler failing to add capacity is the bigger issue. Any provisioning errors?

ops-oncall: Provisioning error: `nodepool-provisioner: insufficient-gpu-resources in az-1` around 10:11. Fallback region not enabled for this pool.

Ashwin (account): Quick billing check — acct-TESS-921 burst_credit_balance before spike: 19600, after spike: 0 at 10:13. Refill schedule shows +1000/min but the traffic consumed credits far faster. They were using dedicated reserved capacity so we should verify committed throughput vs observed.

Customer Support: Customer wants to know why autoscale didn't protect them — they expected reserved pool to scale for burst.

Priya (sre): Root cause hypothesis: noisy traffic spike + autoscale provisioning failure in AZ + conservative headroom + lack of cross-AZ fallback => burst credits burned quickly and admission controller enforced denial. Short-term mitigation suggestions: 1) Increase account burst credits manually to cover immediate replay, 2) enable cross-region fallback for the pool, 3) temporarily lower min_headroom for dp-prod-12 to reduce wasted tokens, 4) ask customer to rate-limit client to preserve tokens.

Evelyn (sales): I'll propose raising burst credits for 24h while we remediate — TesseractPay is on an enterprise commit.

Liam (eng-runtime): To fix autoscale: need to allow pool to spawn in a secondary AZ or fallback to compatible GPU types. I'll open an eng-runtime ticket to enable multi-AZ spillover for dp-prod-12. Also we should lower the headroom algorithm's multiplier for small-request workloads — sending sample histogram now.

Priya (sre): Repro steps I'm running locally to validate:
```
# synthetic burst repro
for i in {1..1200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -d '{"input":"token-test"}' https://dp-prod-12.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
```
Observing admission deny when account credits at 0, and p95 latency climb before that.

Liam (eng-runtime): Can you capture these traces and include X-Request-Id headers? Also paste `admission` and `kvcache` counters.

Priya (sre): Attached partial logs: `10:12:58 admission: allow account=acct-TESS-921 tokens=+1200 headroom_left=3800`, `10:13:12 admission: deny account=acct-TESS-921 reason=burst_credits_exhausted tokens=+0`, `10:13:18 autoscale: spawn_attempt pool=dp-prod-12 status=failed reason=insufficient-gpu-resources az=az-1`

Ashwin (account): Action: I'll authorize a +50k temporary burst credit grant for acct-TESS-921 (expires 2026-03-16T12:00Z).

Customer Support: Customer confirmed burst credits were added and 429s dropped within ~90s. They still want root cause and long-term fix. :thumbsup:

Priya (sre): Next steps assigned:
- Priya: compile post-incident timeline + metrics (TPS, tokens/sec, headroom utilization) — due 2026-03-16 18:00 UTC
- Liam: eng-runtime ticket to enable multi-AZ fallback + headroom tuning for dp-prod-12 — ticket RT-9843
- Ashwin: confirm temporary credit grant and propose commit-level burst policy with customer — due EOD today
- ops-oncall: run a failover test for dp-prod-12 to ensure autoscale can fallback to alternate AZs w/o service window.

Liam (eng-runtime): Also recommending a short-term software workaround: lower `min_headroom_tokens` to 1500 for pools with many small requests, and add a per-pool headroom multiplier derived from request size histogram. I'll include a PR link in the ticket.

Priya (sre): Thanks. I'll update the customer thread with timeline and mitigation steps. Marking this thread as triaged.

Customer Support: Thanks all — customer appreciated the quick patch and the temporary credit. We'll follow up with the post-incident report for closure. :rocket:
